title: Palantir's Report Moved My Buy Price for the Stock. Here's the New Number.
detail:
Palantir's Report Moved My Buy Price for the Stock. Here's the New Number.
Daniel Sparks, The Motley Fool
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 4:07 PM EST 5 min read
PLTR
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

In mid-October, I set a simple rule for buying Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) stock: 120 times the earnings it posted for its last four quarters. Back then, that was around $140 per share, while the stock traded near $198.

I also said that if Palantir's earnings kept rising, my buy price should rise with them.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

They did. Palantir's third-quarter report, released after the market closed on Monday, Nov. 2, lifted those trailing earnings enough to move my number to about $172 per share.

And the stock moved the other way. Shares closed Monday at $178.34 and dropped about 3% after hours to roughly $173 as of this writing. Shares are now down about 17% from their Oct. 9 record close of $209.05 -- and sit only about 1% above my new price.

Image source: Getty Images.

My buy price climbed about 22%

My rule hasn't changed, but the quarters it counts have.

Palantir's third-quarter earnings per share came in at $0.44, up from $0.18 for the third quarter of 2025. With that year-ago quarter now out of the trailing total, the four quarters that count are the fourth quarter of 2025 ($0.24), the first two quarters of 2026 ($0.34 and $0.41), and the latest $0.44. Add them up, and Palantir earned $1.43 a share in the last year. That's around 22% above the $1.17 it had earned when I set the rule. And it's more than three times the $0.42 Palantir earned in the four quarters a year before.

At 120 times earnings, $1.43 a share works out to about $172.

The report also cleared both bars I set for it in an Oct. 31 piece. Revenue climbed 96% year over year to around $2.31 billion, topping the $2.3 billion I'd looked for. And Palantir's sales to American companies (its U.S. commercial revenue) climbed 148% to $984 million, well above the $930 million or so I'd flagged.

Is Palantir's profit growth slowing?

Granted, a buy price linked to earnings only keeps rising if earnings do. And at first glance, the latest quarter looks like a slowdown.

Compared with the quarter before, Palantir's earnings per share grew about 42% at the start of 2026, about 21% in the second quarter, and only about 7% in the third.

But most of that slowdown came from outside the software business itself. Palantir's operating income reached $1.085 billion, up around 19% from $912 million in the second quarter, for a 47% operating margin. It was also almost triple the $393 million the company made from operations in the year-ago quarter.

Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) CEO Alex Karp ended the company's third-quarter earnings call on November 2, 2026 by speaking directly to the stock's skeptics. He was thanking early backers who invested their own money, people who "would otherwise be called retail", when he said: "And part of the delivery here, part of what motivates me is helping to make sure we are fighting for you and, quite frankly, making sure that the people that made fun of you and made fun of us are suffering. And I'm very proud of that, and I'm very proud to have all of you along with us, and thank you for that support."

Drew Angerer/ Getty Images News via Getty Images

Just before that, Karp said those shareholders had "defended us against what obviously now look like ridiculously stupid and malicious, incredibly hard-to-understand attacks," which he called "something that we will never forget."

Results That Back Up Karp's Swagger

Revenue came in at $2.313 billion, up 96% year over year. That is the fastest growth Palantir has delivered as a public company. Growth has picked up every quarter this year, from 84.71% in Q1 to 92.83% in Q2. GAAP net income was $1.128 billion, and the adjusted operating margin expanded to 62% from 51% a year ago.

title: Palantir Stock Falls Despite Earnings Beat as Contract Growth Raises Concerns
detail:
Palantir Stock Falls Despite Earnings Beat as Contract Growth Raises Concerns
Matias Civita
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 2:01 PM EST 3 min read
PLTR
Trade PLTR on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Palantir Technologies delivered another quarter of surging revenue and raised its sales outlook, but investors sent its shares lower as slower contract growth raised questions about whether the artificial intelligence software company can sustain the expectations embedded in its stock price.

Shares fell about 8% to $164.05 in premarket trading Tuesday, despite quarterly sales exceeding Wall Street forecasts. Third-quarter revenue reached $2.313 billion, up 96% from a year earlier and above the approximately $2.18 billion analysts expected. The stock later paired losses, falling a little over 1% at 2 p.m. ET.

Adjusted earnings of 44 cents per share also exceeded the 41-cent consensus estimate. Yet those results were overshadowed by scrutiny of new contracts, a measure investors use to assess the durability of future revenue.

For Patrick Boyle, financial commentator, former hedge fund manager, and university lecturer at King's College London and Queen Mary, University of London, the reaction reflects the expectations attached to one of the market's most expensive large companies. "At that price, investors don't spend much time on the quarter that just ended," Boyle said. "They look for signs of what comes next, and those signs softened."

Boyle put Palantir's valuation at approximately 50 times this year's expected revenue, following a share-price increase of almost 900% over three years. That premium, he argued, makes even modest signs of slowing momentum consequential.

"Palantir's valuation leaves little room for growth to slow," said Jacopo Viganò of GB Capital. "Revenue rose 96% year over year to $2.313 billion, while the value of contracts closed grew 6%. I read the selloff as concern about whether future contract growth can sustain the expectations built into the share price."

Boyle said Palantir's record of exceeding forecasts has also changed how investors judge its results. "So investors stopped asking whether it would beat and started asking by how much," he said. "When everyone expects a beat, a beat becomes the base case."

The company reported $2.918 billion in total contract value closed during the quarter. Within its closely watched U.S. commercial business, contract value increased 11% from a year earlier. Management forecast fourth-quarter revenue between $2.649 billion and $2.653 billion, comfortably exceeding the $2.46 billion analyst estimate.

"Fourth-quarter revenue guidance implies about 15% sequential growth, following 20% in the third quarter," Viganò said. "That is still rapid growth, but it can disappoint shareholders who expect continued acceleration."
